title: The Friday Key
subject: A woman who has wound the town-hall clock every Friday for thirty years is handed a quartz replacement and asks to wind it one last time with the new mayor
caption: Finnish tango iskelma, minor-key schmaltz in the Suomi-tango tradition. Accordion carrying the melody with long legato phrases and sharp staccato dotted rhythm, nylon-string guitar strumming, upright bass walking on the beat, soft brushed snare, small string pad on the chorus. Soft hall reverb, close accordion. Male baritone, rounded warm voice, slightly formal delivery. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 84 BPM, A minor. Wistful, dignified, a little proud. No loud drum kit, no synths, no autotune, no rapping, no electric guitar, no pop beat.
lyrics:
[Intro - accordion, nylon guitar]

[Verse 1]
Every Friday at a quarter past four
I climb the stairs of the old town hall
Ninety steps and a rusted door
The iron key is warm in my hand

[Verse 2]
Thirty years I've turned the crank
Now they bring a box with a battery
They say it never loses a minute

[Chorus]
Let me wind it once more
Before you take the key
Oh, the town will keep its time
But who will keep it kind

[Verse 3]
The new mayor stands beside me
Coat too thin for the cold of the tower
I show him how to lift the lever
He breathes out when it starts

[Bridge - accordion alone, then guitar]
Four chimes, then five
Hold the weight, let it fall

[Chorus]
Let me wind it once more
You may keep the key
Oh, the town will keep its time
And the battery can wait

[Outro - accordion, slow strings]
Ninety steps down
The clock goes on
